newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists mainly neutral for shares.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists mainly neutral for shares.

text.p: Most Dutch chartists are taking a neutral stance on the AEX share index for the current week, after the index fell nearly 33 points last week.
"The AEX is bottoming within the boundaries of its falling trend channel," said ING, and switched from the downtrend (last week) to a neutral stance.
ING added that strong resistance comes in at around last week's peak at 741.
The AEX share index, which was 19.08 points higher at 727.51 at 1330 GMT, was likely to remain choppy in the coming days.
"The short term trend is very volatile," said MeesPierson.
ABN AMRO stuck to the uptrend and advised long positions.
The AEX index closed at 708.43 points on Friday April 4, 32.56 lower than the previous week's close.

Note - Contributors' own analysis follows.

ING BARINGS - The AEX is bottoming within the boundaries of its falling trend channel. A minor base formation, being formed in the 695-700 area, should provide the floor for some upward bounces. Strong resistance comes in at around last week's peak at 741. Intermediate resistance at the falling trend line at 730. For the next few days we expect some upward bounces. A close above the 9-day moving average line at 710 would trigger a minor buy signal. However, for the time being we consider this rally only a mere rebound within the downtrend, unless it breaks above 741, indicating that upward potential is limited.

Money flow of the AEX is slowly picking up, indicating that the influx of new funds has started. The advance/decline line is slowly basing, indicating that winning stocks are outnumbering the losers. We have upgraded our rating to neutral.

MEESPIERSON - The short term trend is very volatile. The technical indicators are still short term to medium term negative, although they are very difficult to read during periods of high volatility because of their lagging character. The market is capped in a trading range between roughly 698 and 742. We still think the risks are on the downside were the market could reach the level of 680 to 660 but it isn't so far yet. The long term uptrend looks still positive.

RABO SECURITIES - We continue to foresee high volatility within a broad trading range 698 - 744. A breach of support at 698 will immediately trigger a sell signal for a move targeting 685. Resistance at 744 is unlikely to be broken this week.

ABN AMRO - Amsterdam has tested the 700 support level for the second time last week, and again this level proved to be the bottom for investors who are focusing on the medium term time frame. Due to a slight overshooting effect, the 700-barrier was broken for a moment which was not confirmed as a significant break through by the objective indicators.

This deviation between the two pictures is referred to as positive divergence, which indicates the presence of upward potential on the short term. This positive divergence is also present in the charts of most individual stocks in Amsterdam. Therefore, we state that the expected upmove is broadly supported by the market. In order to place a more safe trade, we advise to wait for the 726 to be taken out. In this case, the medium term downtrend which was initiated at the top will be broken. Summarising the above, we state that long positions are advised.
Additionally, we advise to increase long exposure above 726 for a ride with the bulls towards 744 level, where the AEX finds its first real resistance. Place a stop just below 720.

JAAD - The computer program has lowered its support levels due to big increases in volatility and remains in a neutral position because of the fact that some indicators are positive and some are negative. Positive is slightly in favour because of a positive divergence between RSI and closing-prices.
